**Final finding: AUDIT — compliant. No redline, no comment.**

The repair is complete; the substance was already correct and the verifier confirmed each element, so I tightened the rationale rather than altering the conclusion.

Basis for the finding:
- **No audit right against us exists.** Literal and regex sweeps (*audit, inspect, verif, examin, right to enter, books, records, premises, access, remote*) plus full reads of § 3, § 14 and § 20 turn up nothing binding Sparkling.
- **§ 3 (p0029–p0035)** contains substantive use restrictions only — no verification, reporting or self-certification mechanic attached.
- **§ 14 (p0095)** — "accounting records for which access is obtained" is definitional scoping within a mutual confidentiality clause, not a grant of access. The only § 10 "access" is Garman's telephone support flowing *to* us.
- **§ 16 escrow (p0114)** is the sole examination right in the document and it runs **in our favour**.

Why no edit: the AUDIT rule caps a Vendor-favourable right, so its absence places us at or better than the preferred position. Inserting frequency/notice/cost parameters would create the very obligation the rule is designed to limit. The failed deterministic check ("audit frequency limited") is an artefact of there being no audit clause to measure, not a defect.

Negotiation note only, not raised with Garman: if a verification right is later proposed, hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct system access.
